20.0.s.en: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

20.0.0.en: Christ continued His positive work of preaching and teaching in the temple, and the opposition of the Jewish leaders to Him did not cease, so the chief priests and elders gathered around Him and asked Him by what authority He worked miracles and taught, and who gave Him this authority.

20.0.1.en: Their question was not for inquiry but to expose His error, for their hearts were filled with envy and malice. They meant that He was not of the tribe of Levi or the descendants of Aaron, who were responsible for the service in the temple, but of the tribe of Judah, so how could He perform this service without having taken permission from the high priest or the civil authority.

20.1.0.en: Christ did not convince them of His divine authority and did not answer them, because their question was an attack to catch Him in an error and not for sound understanding.

20.1.1.en: Therefore Christ replied to them with another question: if they answered Him, He would answer their question. This question was whether the baptism of John was sent from heaven or was a worthless human invention. His question was not an evasion of answering theirs, because if they answered His question by acknowledging John's message and baptism, they would thereby declare their faith in all that John said about Him, namely that He has complete divine authority and is the Judge of the whole world.

20.1.2.en: Keep away from foolish discussions, that is, unprofitable ones, when you are sure of the bad intention of the one who asks or argues, so that you keep your peace.

20.2.0.en: They reasoned with themselves: they stepped aside and consulted how to answer Him, because His question embarrassed them and exposed their error.

20.2.1.en: The leaders felt embarrassed, because if they agreed that it was from heaven, their envy and pride would be exposed, which had kept them from declaring their faith in John's baptism and submitting to him; and on the other hand, if they said it was of men, that is, that John was merely an ordinary man and not sent by God, the Jews would rise against them, because John was in everyone's eyes a great prophet.

20.3.0.en: In their bewilderment and embarrassment, they were forced in shame to declare their ignorance, so they said that they did not know. This meant their weakness and their inability to judge by what authority Christ teaches, because the power of His teaching and His many miracles confirm His divinity, but because of their wickedness they oppose Him. Then Christ said to them, "Neither tell I you," the source of my power. Thus He exposed their weakness and got free of the unprofitable dispute.

20.4.1.en: The vineyard: is mankind and the world which He created.

20.4.2.en: The husbandmen: are the shepherds in the Old Testament, that is, the priests and the leaders of the people, the scribes, Pharisees and lawyers, to whom God entrusted the care of His people.

20.4.3.en: Went into a far country for a long time: that is, He gave them complete freedom throughout their lives; for He is present in every place and time, but He left them to do as they wished as though He were far from them.

20.5.0.en: At the season: it is the time of harvest and gathering the fruits, and it means that after He had given the Jewish priests sufficient opportunity to care for the people and teach them, He sent to ask for the souls who believe in Him and live with Him, that is, He asks for worship, godliness and conduct befitting His children.

20.5.1.en: A servant: conscience, or some of the prophets.

20.5.2.en: Beat him, and sent him away empty: they silenced people's consciences and distorted them and did not respond to God; or they opposed the prophets and wearied them and did not respond to their teachings.

20.5.3.en: After He had left them for a sufficient time, He sent to ask for the virtues, the righteousness and the life of His children, and He sent His servants to demand these fruits.

20.5.4.en: The first servant: is conscience, that is, the voice of God within us calling us to righteousness, but the wicked rejected it and tormented it and did not give it what it called for, like Cain, who rejected the voice of his conscience to love his brother and went on hating him until he killed him. And so it was with all the wicked in the days of Noah and those dwelling in Sodom and Gomorrah.

20.6.0.en: Another servant: is the Law of Moses or another group of prophets.

20.6.1.en: The Jewish priests rejected the Law of Moses by distorting its meanings for their own purposes, and dishonored it by their evil deeds, and did not give it the virtues it asked for, that is, they sent it away empty; or they persisted in rejecting the words of the prophets and dishonoring them.

20.7.0.en: A third: the prophets in general, or the last group of the prophets.

20.7.1.en: The priests persecuted the prophets, tormented them and cast them out by rejecting their words and throwing them into prisons. In sum, mankind rejected the voice of God which He sent in many forms so that they might repent and return to Him.

20.8.0.en: There was nothing left for God but to give them all His love, by sending His only Son Jesus Christ, that perhaps they would respect Him and fear Him because of the power of His words and miracles.

20.9.0.en: Strangely, the Jewish priests and their leaders felt the power of Christ and His authority and the people's following Him, so they feared for their positions and their earthly power, and did not think of the salvation of their people nor of their own souls, and they conspired to be rid of Him and kill Him. Had they not known the power of Christ, they would have had an excuse, but they knew and rejected out of their pride and their desire for authority and positions.

20.10.0.en: And so they crucified Christ outside Jerusalem. And Christ asks the hearers what their judgment is on these wicked husbandmen.

20.10.1.en: It appears from the parable that Christ knew what they would do to Him a few days later, namely His crucifixion outside Jerusalem, yet in His love He accepts the sufferings for our salvation.

20.11.0.en: The hearers declared their distress at these husbandmen, saying, "God forbid" at what they had done. And Christ declares His judgment, that He comes in the New Testament and dwells by His Holy Spirit on His disciples, and takes the care of His people from the Jewish priests and gives it to His disciples and Apostles in the Church. And nothing awaits these husbandmen but destruction and eternal torment.

20.11.1.en: Any sin is forgiven, however grave, except hardness of heart and refusing to obey the Church, that is, refusing God's commandments through self-justification and pride. So take care to repent every day and before your father of confession, and you will mend your faults however grave they are and receive forgiveness and strength for life with God.

20.12.0.en: He reminded them of what is written in the Psalm (Ps 118:22) about Christ who humbled Himself by His Incarnation, likening Him to the stone which the builders rejected, who are the shepherds of the Jewish people, but it became the head of the corner, on which the two walls meeting at one corner depend. The meaning of this is that Christ, whom the Jewish priests rejected, became the salvation of the Jews and the Gentiles and the foundation of the Church.

20.12.1.en: Whoever opposes the incarnate Christ, this stone, is wearied, loses his peace and torments himself; but the more serious thing is that if this stone falls on anyone, at the appearing of Christ in His second coming to judge the world, it will grind to powder all who died refusing to believe in Him.

20.13.0.en: The priests understood that they were the wicked husbandmen, so they tried to arrest Christ, but they feared because of the people's love for Him.

20.13.1.en: Do not become angry with the one who exposes your faults and try to wrong him; he is the voice of God to rescue you from your sins.

20.14.0.en: The priests were unable to arrest Christ, and they tried to catch Him in an error from His own mouth so as to bring Him to trial before the governor, so they sent to Him some Jews who pretended to be righteous and godly.

20.15.0.en: Neither acceptest thou the person of any: you do not favor the persons of the great and change the truth to please them.

20.15.1.en: They approached Him in the spirit of discipleship and praised Him as a teacher of spiritual things who favors no one, in order to deceive Him and make Him fall into an error, and they asked Him whether tribute should be given to Caesar or not. If He agreed, He would be considered a traitor by the Jews, who consider that God is their King and that it is not lawful to give tribute to the Romans; and if He refused to give tribute, He would be considered a stirrer of sedition among the people and would be brought to trial.

20.16.0.en: God, who knows what is in hearts, knew their craftiness and deceit, so He asked for a penny, and asked whose image and inscription was stamped on it on the penny. They said, "Caesar's," and He answered, "Render therefore unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's, and unto God the things which be God's," that is, give money to the world and its authority, but the heart give to God. By this He made clear a Christian principle, which is submission to the authorities and civil laws so that we may be good citizens submissive to the state, yet distinguished by consecrating the heart to God and carrying out His commandments.

20.16.1.en: Would that the image in you were God's, so that you become like Him, and not the world's, so that you please it with sins and lusts.

20.17.0.en: These deceivers felt their helplessness before the wisdom of Christ, so they were silent and marveled at the loftiness of His wisdom and His unexpected answer, which was nevertheless right and profound, because it calls them to the spiritual life and to keep away from foolish discussions or attempts to trap Him in a wrong word.

20.18.s.en: (4) The question about marriage and the resurrection

20.18.0.en: The Sadducees were an aristocratic sect among the Jewish leaders, who believed that when a person dies, his spirit dies as well as his body, that is, they did not believe in the life to come.

20.19.0.en: The Law of Moses required that if someone had no children in his marriage and died, his brother must marry his wife to raise up offspring so that the land of inheritance in Canaan would not be lost, and because all were waiting for the Messiah to come from their descendants.

20.19.1.en: But the Sadducees did not understand and believe in the life to come, and they exploited this law and composed a story, hoping to embarrass Christ with it and convince Him of their opinion, which is that there is no life after death.

20.20.0.en: The story is that a man married a woman and had no children and died, so his brother married her and had no children and died, and so with the rest of the brothers, who were seven, and then the woman died. The Sadducees' question was whose wife the woman would be in the eternal life, if there is life after death, since the woman had married the seven brothers. They thought that if there is life after death, it would be like earth, each husband living with his wife and children.

20.21.0.en: The children of this world: who live on the earth.

20.21.2.en: The resurrection from the dead: those who live in the Kingdom after the last resurrection and the day of judgment. Neither can they die any more: they have no bodies to die, but are spirits.

20.21.3.en: Equal unto the angels: spirits like the angels.

20.21.4.en: The children of God: they are established in their sonship to God, not exposed to falling into sin.

20.21.5.en: The children of the resurrection: those who rose in the last resurrection after the day of judgment and who are immortal in eternity. Christ answered that marriage exists on earth for begetting offspring and preserving the human race, so that it does not become extinct through death, but in heaven they do not die and therefore do not need marriage, but live as spirits like the angels.

20.22.0.en: Then He gave a proof of the existence of life after death, that God, when He spoke to Moses from the bush, called Himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Ex 3:6), and of course these are alive as spirits after death, because God is too great to call Himself by the names of men who died and were buried and no longer have any worth.

20.23.0.en: The scribes, who believe in the life to come, were pleased on hearing Christ's reply, and the Sadducees were unable before Christ's argument and persuasiveness to question Him or oppose Him.

20.23.1.en: Do not oppose the opinions of others and justify your own thinking, but listen and appreciate all opinions, for you may find some benefit in them, or they may be more correct than your own opinion.

20.24.0.en: While Christ was teaching the crowds and sometimes addressing the scribes, Pharisees and Sadducees, He directed His discourse toward His disciples, and it was mostly in the hearing of the scribes and Pharisees. It appears from this discourse, part of which Luke mentions, that Christ was bold and not afraid of the scribes and Pharisees in warning His disciples of their errors, and at the same time, when the scribes and Pharisees heard these words, it was a call for their repentance.

20.25.0.en: Christ warned them against imitating the scribes in the love of greatness and fame, which they pursue out of their pride and for acquiring money, for they were lovers of gathering money.

20.25.1.en: The scribes used to wear long robes (tallit), which are garments reaching to the feet that kings and great men wear, and they rejoiced in people's honoring them in every public gathering such as the marketplaces; and when they entered the synagogues or feasts, they asked to be in the foremost places so that people would glorify them.

20.26.0.en: More than this, in their hypocrisy they meant to prolong their prayers although their hearts were wicked, and they wronged the widows, for Jewish society considered them jurists and trustees whose counsel was sought, and they wrote down people's wills for them before their death, so they exploited this to take their money, especially the money of widows.

20.26.1.en: Because of this hypocrisy, that is, pretending to holiness despite inner wickedness, they receive greater damnation than an ordinary person if he sins, because he may have sinned out of ignorance.

20.26.2.en: In proportion to how much you have known Christ and learned in the Church, be exact in your life and hasten to repentance and confession if you sin.

20.26.3.en: Chapter twenty-one: the signs of the end and watchfulness; the widow's two mites (vv. 1-4):

20.26.5.en: 1- And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury. 2- And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites. 3- And he said, "Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all: 4- for all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had."

21.0.0.en: Christ stood with His disciples near one of the large chests placed in the temple in a special room for offering gifts, and He saw the rich of the Jews casting their gifts into the chest, making a loud ringing because they were metal and in large quantity.

21.1.0.en: Then a poor woman, a widow, came in and cast two mites into the chest quietly, so they made no sound. The mite is the smallest Jewish coin, and the two mites equal one-tenth of a denarius, which is equivalent today to about five Egyptian piasters.

21.2.0.en: Christ praised the woman's gift and even esteemed it above the other gifts, although it was the smallest thing offered in its material value; but in relation to what she had, she gave everything, while the rich, despite the great value they gave, gave a small part of what was left over beyond their needs. For God looks at the measure of love in the heart. The cup of cold water you offer may be greater than great services offered by others, if it is all the effort you have. Therefore do not despise what you can offer to God of prayers, fasts, worship and service, however small, but take care to offer everything you have with love and joy, for it is very precious in His sight. The destruction of the temple (vv. 5-7):

21.2.1.en: This discourse is mentioned in (Mt 24; Mk 13).

21.2.2.en: 5- And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said, 6- "As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down." 7- And they asked him, saying, "Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?"

21.3.0.en: Some: the disciples, as the Gospels of Matthew and Mark relate.

21.3.1.en: The temple of Solomon was adorned with stones and gifts, and they used to renovate its buildings and expected that the Messiah would come and make it His dwelling place, so the disciples stood with Christ praising this great spiritual building, and Christ foretold to them that this building would be torn down and utterly destroyed.

21.4.0.en: The disciples thought, like the rest of the Jews, that this temple would continue until the day of judgment, so they asked Christ about the signs of the end when the temple would be destroyed, and they did not know that it would be destroyed in AD 70 at the hands of the Romans.

21.4.1.en: Do not be dazzled by the delights of the world or let your heart cling to them, for they pass away, but take care to prepare your heart as a temple for God by many prayers, readings and meditations.

21.5.0.en: Christ warned against being attached to the time of His coming, because many will appear in the world to deceive people that He has come in the second coming, whether by declaring themselves to be christs, or founders of schools of thought, or by miracles, like Simon the Magician in the days of the Apostles, or the many heresies that appear to this day, and some of them fix the date of the end of days. Sadly all this is said in the name of Christ, although it has no relation to Him, as He declares in this verse.

21.6.0.en: Among the signs of the approach of the end of the world is the rise of wars between nations and disturbances and revolutions within them... All this declares the instability of the material world, to lift our eyes toward eternity. These wars will recur, but the end is not yet, for there are still many other signs that we shall speak of.

21.7.0.en: Nature will declare its instability in the form of earthquakes in the earth, and troubles in agriculture so that the earth does not give its yield, and famines occur, and diseases spread as pestilences that kill many; and there will even appear upheavals in the sky such as thunder, lightning and storms, declaring the instability of the material heaven, so that we await a new earth and a new heaven in eternity.

21.7.1.en: If a person departs from God, he is shaken as by an earthquake, and hungers for lack of the word of God and of partaking of the sacraments, and bad thoughts spread within him like a plague, and inner conflicts arise between spirit and body, and even his spirit, that is, his heaven, is troubled by many thoughts. Therefore the only solution is to return to God by repentance and to cling to Him.

21.8.0.en: But before all these: before Christ's second coming.

21.8.1.en: They shall lay their hands on you: the arrest of the believers, their trial, imprisonment and torture.

21.8.2.en: They shall persecute you: this means kinds of persecutions and deprivation of rights and various insults.

21.8.3.en: For my name's sake: for the sake of faith in Christ and not for personal faults.

21.8.4.en: When Satan feels the nearness of the Lord's coming, he persecutes the believers, trying to draw them away from the faith, using in this the Jewish synagogues spread through all the lands and the Roman authorities, and he still uses various groups and bodies to persecute the truth in God's children; but their holding fast to their faith bears witness to the truth of what they believed, and declares the loftiness and power of Christianity.

21.9.0.en: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before: do not worry about what you will answer to the persecutions and troubles the wicked cause you.

21.9.1.en: A mouth and wisdom: the word of God on the tongue of the Christians before the persecutors, which silences them and shows their wickedness. Christ reassures us that He will work in us when the wicked persecute us, and give us wisdom and power that show their weakness, because it is His divine power which cannot be overcome, as happened on the lips of the martyrs, who showed the helplessness of those who persecuted them, and many non-Christians believed because of that and were even martyred for Christ's sake, and sometimes the governors themselves and the persecutors believed and were martyred.

21.9.2.en: Trust in the power of God within you when you face a difficult situation or pressures from the world. Only pray and hold fast to God, and He will defend you.

21.10.0.en: Christ warns us that persecution comes not only from strangers or enemies but also from the nearest of the near, such as family members, relatives and friends. When a member of the family believes in Christ, the others persecute him, or when a person holds fast to the Church, those around him oppose him because they do not value the spiritual life, until a person sometimes feels that everyone hates him, so that the devil makes him doubt the possibility of succeeding in his life in the midst of the world.

21.11.0.en: On the other hand, Christ declares that all these persecutions cannot harm us except by His permission, according to our endurance, so that they cannot hurt even one hair of our heads. He asks only that we hold fast to the faith and be patient in these afflictions, and so we win for ourselves eternal salvation. Do not be troubled if everyone around you opposes you. Be humble, bear with them and treat them with love, and return to the Church and your father of confession to be sure of what you hold, and trust that God supports you.

21.12.s.en: (5) The siege and destruction of Jerusalem

21.12.0.en: Christ prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem, which was accomplished in AD 70 at the hands of Titus the Roman, and its siege two years before, and this is a declaration that its destruction had drawn near.

21.13.0.en: The Jews crucified Christ and refused to believe in Him, and He gave them an opportunity afterward of about 40 years, but they did not repent and believe, so the Lord was angry and destroyed Jerusalem, as is written by the prophets such as Daniel and Zechariah (Dan 9:26-27) (Zech 11; 14:1-2), that perhaps they would understand and repent afterward. And He advises His believing children dwelling in Jerusalem to flee from it, and those in the land of Judea around Jerusalem to flee to the mountains so that the Romans do not kill them.

21.13.1.en: The Christians obeyed Christ's warning, and history records that none of them was killed in the destruction of Jerusalem, because they fled quickly before the siege was completed.

21.14.0.en: During the flight from Jerusalem the weak stumble, such as pregnant women and nursing mothers carrying their infants. They signify the spiritually weak, because they stumble when they flee from evil, so they fall into lusts and perish.

21.14.1.en: And the Gentile Romans will trample Jerusalem and kill those in it, and take them captive and carry them away to their lands. And Jerusalem will remain in turmoil and weariness until the Gentiles believe in Christ, and in the end Israel will believe, as St. Paul the Apostle explained (Rom 11:25-26).

21.14.2.en: If only you would grow strong spiritually in times of rest and be bound to the Church, so that when affliction befalls you, you are not troubled but flee to God and call upon Him for help, and so pass through in peace and do not fall into sin.

21.15.0.en: Before Christ's coming, signs appear in the sun, moon and stars, that is, there will be disturbing natural phenomena evident to all mankind, and they appear also on land and sea and cause general distress to all people, so that when everything around them shakes, they repent and prepare for eternity. When the nations are perplexed by these phenomena and grow weary of the distress and anguish surrounding them, they return to God... and great fear covers people because of the disasters that have occurred and what could occur even more than this in the heavenly bodies.

21.15.1.en: When you see or hear of changes in nature, know that you are nearing the end, so repent and prepare.

21.16.0.en: When all the preceding signs are completed, Christ comes from heaven in splendor and majesty with His Cross on the clouds, in intense brightness, appearing to the whole world.

21.17.0.en: Look up, and lift up your heads: be filled with hope, vigor and earnest striving.

21.17.1.en: He charges His believing children, when they see these signs and the appearing of Christ, to be strengthened in spiritual striving, because their redemption from the body has drawn nigh, as Christ takes them to His heavenly Kingdom.

21.17.2.en: Be persevering in your striving all day long to the last moment of your life, because the devil does not rest in his warfare until you are established in your victories and receive eternal glory, and do not be alarmed at your falls, but rise quickly, confident of God's power which supports you, until He takes you to the Kingdom He has prepared for you.

21.18.0.en: Just as we know from the appearance of fruit on the fig tree that summer has come, so also we know the seasons of the year from the fruits of the trees; so when the preceding signs occur, we know that the coming of the Lord is near.

21.19.0.en: Christ also prophesies that the destruction of Jerusalem will take place in this generation. And indeed some of the hearers lived until they saw the destruction of Jerusalem.

21.19.1.en: And Christ affirms that every word He said will be fulfilled, for heaven and earth shall pass away, but the word of God which He has declared to us shall not pass away forever, but we continue to live by it in the heavenly Kingdom.

21.19.2.en: If God's word is sure, then take care to read the Holy Bible and to keep the commandment in your heart and apply it in your life, and you will live forever.

21.20.0.en: After Christ's discourse about the destruction of Jerusalem and the signs of the end of days, affirming that we should not be preoccupied with calculating the time of His coming, He declared the summary of His discourse, which is to beware of being preoccupied with the delights and cares of the world, so that we lose our reason and our purpose and are like those drunk with wine, and do not prepare for the day of judgment, which comes upon us unawares when we are unprepared.

21.21.0.en: Christ declares that the day of judgment will come suddenly like the snare of the hunter into which the prey falls without feeling it. And all mankind will be subject to it, and therefore all must prepare by spiritual alertness.

21.22.0.en: Pray always: prayers and spiritual striving.

21.22.1.en: All these things that shall come to pass: the signs mentioned before, which befall mankind before the day of judgment, and they do not affect God's children or disturb them if they hold fast to Him and are prepared at all times.

21.22.2.en: To stand before the Son of man: the last judgment.

21.22.3.en: Christ offers the only solution for escaping the day of judgment, which is spiritual watchfulness, that is, guarding against the sources of sin and rising from it by repentance if we fall into it, with our hearts occupied with prayers and the relationship with God, so that we grow accustomed to being with Him and do not fear facing Him on the day of judgment, but rejoice because He delivers us from the toils of the world and lifts us to the Kingdom.

21.22.4.en: Put before your eyes at the beginning of each day that you will die and face God, and so be careful in all your actions, words and thoughts, and live with Him and enjoy His fellowship, and thus be prepared at all times, and no longer fear death or the last judgment.
